test_title: SSC Selection Post 2025 (Graduate Level) Official Paper (Held On: 29 Jul, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which of these missions will put India among the select few nations having technology for reusable launch vehicles?
solution:
The correct answer is __**RLV-LEX**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• **RLV-LEX** stands for **Reusable Launch Vehicle Autonomous Landing Mission**. It is a landmark mission by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** designed to develop technologies for a fully reusable rocket. **Hence, this option is correct.**

• The mission was successfully conducted on **April 2, 2023**, at the **Aeronautical Test Range (ATR)** in **Chitradurga**, **Karnataka**. This feat made **India** one of the few nations, alongside the **USA**, **Russia**, and **China**, to master autonomous landing technology for space vehicles.

• **SPOT-7** is a high-resolution **Earth observation satellite** from **France**, launched by **India** in **2014** using the **PSLV-C23** rocket. It is a commercial satellite mission and does not involve reusable launch vehicle technology. **Hence, this option is incorrect.**

• **PSLV-C58** is an expendable launch mission that successfully placed the **XPoSat** (X-ray Polarimeter Satellite) into orbit on **January 1, 2024**. It uses traditional rocket technology where the stages are not recovered. **Hence, this option is incorrect.**

• **RISAT-2** is an **Indian** radar imaging satellite launched in **2009** to provide all-weather surveillance and disaster management support. It is an orbital asset rather than a launch vehicle technology demonstrator. **Hence, this option is incorrect.**

**Additional Information__**
__

• The **RLV-TD** (Technology Demonstrator) program is a series of experimental missions by **ISRO** aimed at developing a **Two-Stage-to-Orbit (TSTO)** fully reusable launch vehicle.

• The primary objective of developing **RLV** technology is to achieve **low-cost access to space**. By reusing the launch vehicle multiple times, the cost of space missions can be reduced by nearly **80%**.

• During the **RLV-LEX** experiment, a prototype named **Pushpak** was carried to an altitude of **4.5 km** by an **Indian Air Force Chinook helicopter** and released mid-air to simulate a vehicle returning from space.

• The vehicle utilized advanced indigenous technologies, including a **Radar Altimeter**, **Pseudolite** navigation system, and **Integrated Navigation, Guidance, and Control** systems to land autonomously on a runway.

• The landing occurred at a high speed of approximately **350 km/h**, demonstrating the precision of **India's** aerospace engineering and autonomous control software.

**Important Points__**

• On **March 22, 2024**, **ISRO** successfully completed the **RLV-LEX-02** mission, which was the second autonomous landing test. This mission tested the vehicle's ability to correct its flight path and land under more challenging initial conditions.

• The **Pushpak** vehicle is equipped with **Thermal Protection Systems (TPS)** to protect its structure from the intense heat generated during atmospheric re-entry from orbit.

• The success of these missions is a critical stepping stone toward the **Orbital Re-entry Experiment (ORE)**, where a vehicle will be launched into orbit and then brought back to land on a designated runway.

• Developing reusable rockets is a global trend, with organizations like **SpaceX** already utilizing reusability to dominate the commercial launch market. **India's** progress ensures it remains competitive in the global space economy.
